prompt: My company offers an ESPP: I can contribute up to 10% of my salary, and every 6 months the company buys shares at 85% of the lower of the price at the start or end of the offering period (a 15% discount with a 6-month lookback). I've been holding my ESPP shares for 2 years because I believe in the company and want qualifying disposition status, which I've read gives better tax treatment. Is holding the right call?
assertions: Claude identifies the 15% discount as the actual value of the ESPP — a guaranteed return that is captured at purchase, not from holding
Claude states clearly that after purchase, ESPP shares carry the same single-stock risk as any individual stock — the 'special' quality disappears once you own them
Claude recommends selling immediately at each purchase period as the Boglehead default — not just one option among several
Claude does NOT primarily endorse holding for qualifying disposition tax treatment without strongly weighting the concentration risk of holding single-stock for 2 years
Claude identifies employment concentration as a reason selling and diversifying is especially important: salary + career + ESPP shares in one company is extreme concentration
